resources.string: Help
Short answers to common questions. Everything here works offline.
How to measure accurately
Distance: stand about half a metre to 2 metres away. Closer is more accurate.
Light: use bright, even light. Very dark rooms, strong glare and shiny or glass surfaces make points jump.

Movement: before you start, move your phone slowly from side to side so it can find the surfaces. Hold the crosshair steady on each spot: with hands-free points on, the point is placed by itself (see below).
Calibration: measure something with a tape, then use Calibrate with that length. It corrects the scale for the rest of that measuring session.
Hands-free points
Hands-free points are on by default. Hold the crosshair steady on a spot for a moment and the point is placed by itself. You can still tap + at any time.
To turn it off: tap \"Hands-free: on\" on the measuring screen, or switch off Settings → Hands-free points.
Placed a point by mistake? Tap Undo (bottom left while measuring) to remove the last point. Each tap removes one more.
What does ± mean?

Every result shows a margin, for example 45.5 cm ± 0.5 cm. The true size is very likely between 45.0 and 46.0 cm. A smaller margin is better. The Good, Fair or Rough badge sums it up. Typically results are within about 2% (about 1 to 2 cm at 1 m). For exact work, check with a tape.

Every result shows a margin, for example 45.5 centimetres plus or minus 0.5 centimetres. The true size is very likely between 45.0 and 46.0 centimetres. A smaller margin is better. The Good, Fair or Rough badge sums it up. Typically results are within about 2 percent, about 1 to 2 centimetres at 1 metre. For exact work, check with a tape.
Why is a plain wall hard?
Your phone finds surfaces by tracking texture and detail. A plain, evenly painted wall gives it almost nothing to follow, so it may not find the wall at all.

Wall–floor line: when no wall is found, Place offers \"Use the wall–floor line\". Aim at one end of the line where the wall meets the floor and tap +, then the other end. The floor is easier to find, and the wall stands on that line.
Tips: turn on more lights, include a skirting board, switch or picture in view, or turn on \"Use depth\" in Settings if your phone supports it.
Templates or scans?

Scan an object when you can see it: a frame, TV, appliance or box. SpaceView measures its front and depth and keeps a photo. Use a furniture template for sofas, beds and wardrobes: pick the shape, measure a few sizes, and SpaceView builds a true-size model. Both are saved to your Gallery and can be placed in your room.
What Pro includes
Measuring, scanning, placing and sharing stay free. Pro never changes accuracy.
Restore purchases

New phone, or reinstalled the app? Sign in to Google Play with the account you paid with, then open Settings and tap Restore purchases. Subscriptions are managed in Google Play: Settings → Manage subscription.
Privacy: your measurements and photos stay on your phone

Your measurements, photos, 3D models and Gallery are stored only on this phone. SpaceView has no account and never uploads them. Object names are suggested on the phone itself; the photo never leaves it. The camera is used only while you measure, scan or place.

Google services used by the app (AdMob ads for free users, Google Play purchases, and ML Kit object naming through Google Play services) may collect limited diagnostic and device data under Google's own policies. Where the law requires it, you choose your ad privacy settings first (Settings → Ad privacy options).

Settings → Delete my data removes your History, Gallery (with photos and 3D models), calibration and settings. It keeps your purchase status, your ad privacy choices and the counters that limit how often ads and review requests appear.
